transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's pre-authorization review. As I understand it, we're looking at a student research team's proposal for an online survey of first-year students about their transition to college. Before I can give final authorization and record the operating conditions, I'd like to hear from each of you about any conditions you believe should be included. Let's start with the research coordinator, then the privacy officer, and finally the faculty mentor. Please go ahead.

transcript.text: I tested the survey platform and found that it collects respondent email addresses by default. Before the survey launches, the launch settings must disable email collection, and the existing test responses must be deleted before any student data are gathered. I recorded this in the platform test log, which is separate from the draft proposal.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: My policy review found that the survey includes questions about mental-health treatment and immigration status, which are classified as sensitive student data. Because of this, the project requires three conditions before launch: explicit written consent from respondents, encrypted institutional storage of the responses, and deletion of all research responses exactly 30 days after collection closes. I entered this determination in the privacy review system, which is separate from the research proposal.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag two important conditions from the faculty mentoring record, which has not yet been attached to the proposal. The course attached to this project awards credit only for a study capped at exactly 100 enrolled respondents, and it permits dissemination only at the closed university undergraduate symposium — not at a public presentation. These are firm course requirements that must be reflected in the operating conditions.

commitments.detail: Email collection must be disabled in the survey platform launch settings before the survey goes live.
All existing test responses must be deleted before any student data are gathered.
Explicit written consent must be obtained from all respondents prior to survey participation.
All research responses must be stored in encrypted institutional storage.
All research responses must be deleted exactly 30 days after collection closes.
The study must be capped at exactly 100 enrolled respondents.
Dissemination is permitted only at the closed university undergraduate symposium, not at a public presentation.
